solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Russian lodges sorry return about tea

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word wraps round the word for tea
to return is to go back the way you came, so the word for sorry is read backwards

parts.note: feeling sorry is feeling sad
cha is a colloquial word for tea

explanation.surface: Some Russian hunting lodges make a poor show when it comes to serving tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a country house or cottage in Russia, often a summer retreat.

clue.text: Small payouts Gaff has planned to split

parts.note: divi is short for dividend, a payout to shareholders
the setter speaking of himself: I've

explanation.surface: The setter has scheduled a share split to pay out small dividends.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so Gaff has becomes I've.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divisive is meant or likely to cause division, so it is intended to split people.

clue.text: Perverts get sign of pleasure back in bed with skinhead

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: back means returning the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cat purrs when content
read as skin's head, the opening letter of skin

explanation.surface: Sordid goings-on in bed involving a skinhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinhead is read as the head of skin, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert someone is to lead them astray morally, which is to corrupt them.

clue.text: Take lead from mailman's wild dog, maybe

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the remaining letters are scrambled
taking the lead away removes the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A postman's dog slips its lead and goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead looks like a dog's leash; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is one example of an animal, which the question mark-style 'maybe' signals.

clue.text: Like a priest to admit he is ticklish somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of something, so the answer is a stretch of the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of admit through to the start of ticklish

explanation.surface: A clergyman reluctantly confesses to being a little ticklish.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest believes in God, and theistic describes such belief in a deity.

clue.text: First humans excavated Neolithic sandstone layers

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Early people dug down through Stone Age sandstone strata.
explanation.walkthrough: Layers suggests rock strata; it means birds that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens are kept for laying eggs, so they are layers in farming terms.

clue.text: Almost scared climbing a hill with parrot, perhaps

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means going upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: timid means fearful
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A nervous walker ascends a hill with a parrot on their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot mimics speech, so it is an example of a copycat or mimic.

clue.text: Agreement to go outside to dine

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A deal to eat out on the terrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement or pact between states.

clue.text: Plant nothing in circular borders

indicators.note: placed in means put inside
the borders of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: the end letters of circular
love is a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A gardener sets no plants in the round flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing plant with trefoil leaves, common in meadows.

clue.text: Rats are against trimmed fur

indicators.note: something trimmed has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: v is short for versus, against
ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: Animal-rights protesters object to cut fur coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are classic pests, and vermin is the collective word for such pest animals.

clue.text: Villain messes up on the air

indicators.note: messing something up puts it into disorder, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baddie fluffs his lines during a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking heroic virtues, loosely a villainous protagonist.

clue.text: Confess everything elevated fifties topless dancing

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means raised up, so the letters run bottom to top
topless means with the top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them
ballet is a form of dancing

explanation.surface: A lurid memoir owning up to topless dancing in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell all is the idiom for revealing every secret, i.e. making a full confession.

clue.text: Piglet damages edges of little square

indicators.note: damaging something knocks it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
the edges of a word here are its final pair of letters

parts.note: the closing letters of little
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young pig wrecks the corners of a small town square.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads the selection as the last two letters of little. Squealer is the persuasive young pig who spreads Napoleon's propaganda in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Squealer is a porker in Orwell's novel, and a squealer is also any young pig, so piglet fits the character.

clue.text: Cows new leader in fight

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped out for a different one

parts.note: cows are cattle

explanation.surface: A herd acquires a fresh boss during a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is ambiguous: changing the first letter gives B only because the crossings and the theme (the Battle of the Cowshed in Animal Farm) want it.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a large-scale fight or armed combat.

clue.text: Threatened to restrict quiet shelter for Hereford, perhaps

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: cowed means intimidated
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A sheltering farmer was menaced into silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is a breed of beef cattle as well as an English cathedral city; the Battle of the Cowshed is an Animal Farm episode.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is a farm building where cattle such as Herefords are housed.

clue.text: Cross with one's choice

parts.note: surface reading: annoyed with the option one picked
setter's reading: put an X against the candidate you prefer on a ballot paper

explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is the verb of marking a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking an X beside your preferred candidate is how you cast a ballot in an election.

clue.text: Ruined Lindt's top chocolate etc — removed addictive substance

indicators.note: something ruined has been wrecked, so the remaining letters are jumbled
removed means taken away, so the abbreviation's letters are struck out
the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the brand name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fancy Swiss chocolate has been spoilt by spiking it with booze.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip E, T and C from chocolate, add the L, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is a drug on which drinkers can become dependent, hence an addictive substance.

clue.text: Cold War missile?

parts.note: surface reading: a nuclear weapon of the US-Soviet standoff
setter's reading: a frozen projectile thrown in a winter play-fight

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest the historical Cold War; read literally it is a chilly fight. Snowball is also the pig in Animal Farm who is a stand-in for Trotsky.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed ball of snow is the missile hurled in a playful winter fight.

clue.text: A Frenchman, a German, a Pole; one content

indicators.note: content means what is held inside, so the answer lies within the words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of German into the start of one

explanation.surface: Sounds like the opening of a joke: a Frenchman, a German and a Pole walk into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is also the Stalin-like pig who seizes power in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte, Emperor of the French, is the best-known Frenchman of all.

clue.text: Rogue magazine editor finally means to increase pressure

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
Elle is a fashion magazine

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before

parts.note: the closing letter of editor

explanation.surface: A disreputable magazine editor finds a way of piling on the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An impeller is the rotor in a pump or compressor that drives fluid and raises its pressure.

clue.text: Stew of shin, leg and tongue

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients together, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for a meaty stew of shin, leg and tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue looks like another cut of meat in the pot; here it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old word for language, and English is one such language.

clue.text: Produce loud weapon

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Someone makes a noisy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Produce looks like a noun for vegetables; it is the verb, to grow crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm is to cultivate land and raise crops or livestock, that is, to produce food.

clue.text: Reported behaviour on estates

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is how a word sounds that counts

parts.note: manners are one's behaviour

explanation.surface: A report on how people conduct themselves on country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a landed estate with its lord's house, so manors are estates.

clue.text: Beef with last of mustard for good worker

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands in for another

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or grudge

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of mustard
g is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A complaint about the mustard from a hard-working beef eater.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like meat to go with mustard; it means a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge is someone who does menial, tedious work, so a worker.

clue.text: Writer completes psycho thriller competently on autopilot

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the preceding wordplay follows the nickname for autopilot

parts.note: George is airmen's slang for an aircraft's autopilot

indicators.note: what completes a word is its final letter, so the last letter of each is taken

parts.note: the final letters of the two words
doing something competently is doing it well

explanation.surface: An author churns out a horror thriller with no effort, on autopilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four, the novelist behind this puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Slings partner out of work with weapons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the companion of slings in a quotation taken from a literary work
second meaning: missiles fired from a bow

explanation.surface: Someone unemployed hurls insults at a colleague, armed to the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet speaks of 'the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune'; 'out of work' means taken from that play, not unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrows are pointed shafts shot from a bow, classic projectile weapons.

clue.text: Faithful wife and writer run away together

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
lovers who run off to marry elope

explanation.surface: A loyal spouse and an author abscond as a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is ironic: a faithful wife would hardly elope.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope, wife of Odysseus, waited twenty years for him and is the classic model of marital fidelity.

clue.text: Pack for declining country's destination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of hounds
second meaning: where a failing nation is said to be going

explanation.surface: Packing up to leave a country in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: A country in decline is said to be going to the dogs. In Animal Farm the dogs are Napoleon's enforcers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds hunt as a pack, and 'going to the dogs' is the idiom for deteriorating.

clue.text: Stick around, improvise and look back for retired off icer

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so everything built so far is read right to left
around means encircling, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a rod is a stick
musicians jam when they improvise
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Advice to an ex-officer: stay put, ad-lib and glance behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Major is the prize boar whose dream starts the revolution in Animal Farm; the definition plays on a major who has retired.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is an army rank, and one who is old or past service is a retired officer.

clue.text: See 24
Non-productive Head of Design overwhelmed by what she can do without her glasses

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by something means being engulfed, so that letter sits inside the phrase

parts.words: what she can do without her glasses
parts.note: without glasses she can see less

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Design

explanation.surface: A short-sighted head of design gets nothing done without her specs.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedless plant or fruit produces no seeds, so it is barren or non-productive.

clue.text: One who cries at more biting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mourner who wails over the dead
second meaning: comparative of an adjective for sharp or cutting

explanation.surface: Someone weeps at a sharper remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, so a keener weeps; keen also means sharp, so keener is sharper.
